title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1966 letter to Tate on Dieudonné crystals. In it, Grothendieck attaches to a p-torsion (truncated Barsotti–Tate) group G over S a Dieudonné crystal M = D*(G). He also sets up a 'duality triangle' ℓ^G → Δ(G) → ℓ̌^{G*}[1] →. Here ℓ^G is the co-Lie complex (cotangent complex along the unit section) of G, G* is the Cartier dual, and Δ(G) is the value of the crystal mod p on S (ε*(M/p)). This triangle is the derived form of the Hodge filtration 0 → ω_G → D(G)_S → Lie(G*) → 0.

Page 72 treats the two extreme cases, étale and multiplicative.

(1) Étale case, continued from p.71.
- Since G is étale, its co-Lie complex vanishes: ℓ^G = 0.
- The triangle therefore degenerates to an isomorphism Δ(G) ≅ ℓ̌^{G*}[1]. In other words, the Hodge filtration gives no extra structure on the crystal M.
- Explicitly, ℓ̌^{G*}[1] ≅ Δ(G) ≅ ε*(M/p) = RHom_Z(G, O_S) ≅ Ǧ ⊗^L_Z O_S ≅ (Ǧ ⊗^L_Z F_p) ⊗_{F_p} O_S, where Ǧ = Hom(G, Q_p/Z_p) is the Pontryagin dual.
- So Δ(G) is a two-term complex. For a truncated BT group of level n, its cohomology sheaves are Ǧ/p ⊗ O_S and Ǧ[p] ⊗ O_S, locally free of the same rank.

(2) Multiplicative type, killed by a power of p.
- G is determined by its Cartier dual G*, which is étale and killed by p^n, so the étale analysis of p.71 applies.
- One sets D*(G) = D_*(G*). On a thickening S' this is D*(G)_{S'} = G*_{S'} ⊗_{Z_p} O_{S'}, where G*_{S'} is the unique étale lift of G* to S'.
- Verschiebung V: D*(G) → D*(G^{(p)}) = D*(G)^{(p)} is the isomorphism induced by the relative Frobenius f_{G*}: G* → G*^{(p)}, which is an isomorphism because G* is étale.
- F is then determined by V through FV = VF = p.
- Consequence: an equivalence between truncated BT groups of level n of multiplicative type and locally free crystals of finite type on S/Λ_n with V an isomorphism.
- The next page (p.73) gives the dual degeneration: ℓ̌^{G*}[1] = 0 and ℓ^G ≅ Δ(G) ≅ G* ⊗^L O_S. It then starts computing Hom between étale and multiplicative groups via F-V-crystals.

Purpose: these are the 'trivial' test cases of the Dieudonné-crystal anti-equivalence and of the Hodge-filtration/deformation dictionary. Étale means F is an isomorphism; multiplicative means V is an isomorphism.
errors: Possible shift-convention slip: for G étale p-torsion one has RHom_Z(G, Z) ≅ Ǧ[-1]. So RHom_Z(G, O_S) ≅ (Ǧ ⊗^L O_S)[-1] rather than Ǧ ⊗^L O_S, unless Δ and ℓ are normalized with a shift. This is harmless given the bracket [1] on ℓ̌^{G*}, but the chain of isomorphisms is written loosely.

The covariance/contravariance conventions (D* versus D_*, which of F or V is the isomorphism, and the twists ^{(p)}) are stated without verification. The previous page carries a marginal 'vérifier'. Within the page the conventions are consistent with the standard ones: étale means F bijective, multiplicative means V bijective.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification of the étale and multiplicative special cases of the crystalline Dieudonné anti-equivalence and of the Hodge triangle. All of this was later published by Grothendieck himself (Montréal 1970), Messing, Illusie and Berthelot–Breen–Messing. Its only interest is historical: an early (1966-era) use of the co-Lie complex duality triangle.
transcription_corrections: '𝒪_*(G^*)' should read 𝔻_*(G^*) (the covariant crystal of the étale dual): D*(G) = D_*(G*).
'𝒪_*(𝔉_{G^*} : G^* → G^{*(p)})' should read D_*(f_{G*}), the crystal map induced by the relative Frobenius f_{G*}.
'Comme ℓ^G_· = 0' — the superscript is G (the étale group itself), with a dot subscript denoting the complex.
Last line: likely 'avec V un isom. (et F déterminé)' or '(et F nilpotent)'; the tail is illegible.
